extracted.intended_audience: school and postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and final-regulation guidance explaining recipients' and employees' obligations under §106.44(c) (notification/mandatory reporting), related confidentiality, training, and Title IX Coordinator duties for K–12 and postsecondary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee notification requirement (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee must notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that “reasonably” may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX “or this part.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees are required to respond to conduct or information that could reasonably meet the definition; they are not required to determine whether the conduct meets every aspect of the regulation's definition (e.g., all elements of hostile environment harassment). If an employee directly witnesses such conduct under the recipient's program or activity, the employee must report the information to the Title IX Coordinator or provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and complaint procedures to the person subjected to the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on scope of sex discrimination (§106.8(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train all employees on the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination under Title IX, including sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training should enable employees to recognize when reported or observed information reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. The Department believes training will reduce speculative reporting and ensure appropriate reporting of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee definition and duties (§106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must define and designate confidential employees and require confidential employees to explain to any person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination the circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(d)(1) requires recipients to notify all participants how to contact confidential employees. §106.44(d)(2) requires confidential employees to explain their confidential status, how to contact the Title IX Coordinator, that the Coordinator may offer/support supportive measures, and the limits on reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on disclosure of personally identifiable information (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(j) generally prohibits disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with this part, except in limited circumstances (e.g., to a parent, guardian, or other authorized legal representative who has the legal right to receive disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures necessary for the recipient to address sex discrimination in its education program or activity are permitted under §106.44(j)(3) to carry out the purposes of 34 CFR part 106. The provision protects personal information of all students, including LGBTQI+ students and students who are pregnant, subject to the specified exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination content requirements (§106.8(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide a notice of nondiscrimination to students, parents/guardians of K–12 students, employees, applicants, and unions/organizations that includes how to report conduct that may constitute sex discrimination and how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must also include how to locate the recipient's nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures. Recipients may include information about employees' notification duties and confidential employees, but the Department declines to require posting internal reporting protocols online, leaving recipients flexibility in implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator receipt and follow-up duties (§106.44(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified, the Title IX Coordinator must offer and, if accepted, coordinate supportive measures and must notify the complainant (or reporter) of grievance procedures and available informal resolution options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(f)(1)(ii) requires offering/supportive measures under §106.44(g). §106.44(f)(1)(iii)(A) requires notifying the complainant of grievance procedures (§106.45, §106.46) and informal resolution (§106.44(k)). The Coordinator may initiate a complaint only in limited circumstances and must consider a complainant's request not to proceed (§106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of complainant autonomy and institutional duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifying the Title IX Coordinator does not eliminate complainant autonomy; complainants retain the ability to decide whether to file a complaint, and the Coordinator must consider a complainant's wishes when determining whether to initiate a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator initiation of a complaint after a complainant declines is contemplated only in very limited circumstances and must weigh factors including the complainant's request not to proceed. The regulations were constructed to balance autonomy and adequate institutional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction for elementary and secondary schools (§106.44(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For elementary and secondary school recipients, all employees who are not confidential employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects the supervisory/control role of K–12 employees and aligns with mandatory State child-abuse reporting responsibilities. The word “reasonably” and reference to “this part” were added to clarify scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary two-category approach (§106.44(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For recipients other than elementary/secondary schools (including postsecondary), non-confidential employees are divided into Category 1 and Category 2: Category 1 (authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising) must notify the Title IX Coordinator; Category 2 (other non-confidential employees) must either notify the Coordinator or provide Coordinator contact info and complaint procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient may require Category 2 employees to do either action or leave that discretion to the employees. This streamlined approach aims to give greater weight to complainant autonomy at postsecondary institutions while ensuring appropriate notice to the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: No distinction between student and employee complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not differentiate notification obligations based on whether the person subjected to the conduct is a student or an employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed distinctions to simplify understanding and implementation so employees know what to do regardless of the reporter's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee witness reporting obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who directly witnesses conduct in the recipient's program or activity that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination is considered to have information and must report or provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information to the person subjected to the conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that direct observation triggers the same notification duty as receiving information from a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility to designate Title IX Coordinator(s) and oversight (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may have more than one Title IX Coordinator and may designate employees to carry out some duties, but the recipient must designate one Coordinator to retain ultimate oversight to ensure consistent compliance with Title IX responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation is permitted, but ultimate responsibility remains with the designated Coordinator to oversee compliance and consistent implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for age-appropriate/contextual assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations of whether conduct constitutes hostile environment sex-based harassment must consider context, including parties' ages and maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees (e.g., teachers) should draw on required training and exercise professional judgment, taking into account minors' immaturity where appropriate; the regulations allow contextual assessment rather than rigid application.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment and academic freedom consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification requirements do not violate the First Amendment; Title IX protects against invidious discrimination and is not intended to regulate constitutionally protected speech. Academic discourse generally would not meet the standard for sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reaffirms commitment to freedom of speech and academic freedom; the preamble references the First Amendment discussion in the definition of “sex-based harassment” (§106.2). The regulations do not require recipients to restrict rights protected from government action by the First Amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process protections for respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification under §106.44(c) does not impair a respondent's due process rights; not all reports will result in investigations, and grievance procedures (§106.45 and §106.46) provide a fair process for respondents when investigations lead to grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees that the reporting requirement will lead to over-reporting that harms due process; investigation and grievance procedures include measures designed to protect respondents' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on posting reporting protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to post their reporting protocols online, preferring to leave recipients flexibility to meet notice requirements through other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may nonetheless include notification duties and confidential-employee information in their notice of nondiscrimination or nondiscrimination policy, but posting detailed protocols is not mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion on Category 2 employee actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For Category 2 employees at non-K–12 recipients, the recipient may decide whether such employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator or instead provide the Coordinator's contact information and complaint procedures, or leave the choice to the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discretion is intended to reduce confusion, administrative burden, and retraining needs when employees' duties shift, while still ensuring pathways for complainants to contact the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to inform individuals of supportive resources and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees and Title IX Coordinators must inform complainants (or reporters) about confidential resources, supportive measures, and options for filing complaints or initiating informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear communication about available supportive measures and procedures supports complainant autonomy and may enable addressing incidents consistent with complainant preferences.
